first_impression.reaction: Sophie sent it, so I'll read all of it. The opening is calm and plain, no silly slang: "A sand ceremony asks very little of you on the day, which is exactly why the words around it matter." Fine. It's really one for her and the celebrant, but I wanted to see whether the parents are in it, and whether anyone mentions the practical side of doing this overseas.

journey.quote: A sand ceremony is a symbolic ritual, so in Australia the legal words under sections 45 and 46 of the Marriage Act 1961 still have to be said around it.
journey.reaction: Good. I like being told straight away that the sand is just the pretty bit and the legal part still has to be done properly. That's the sort of thing I'd worry about.

journey.quote: The pour sits well after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order.
journey.reaction: I read 'well after' as 'a long while after' the first time and had to go back over it. Does it mean straight after, or later on? I'd be asking my husband what they mean.

journey.quote: Their parents, [Names] and [Names], have been invited to begin this pour, one colour from each family.
journey.reaction: Oh, that's lovely. I'd like to do this with Sophie's father. I'll forward this bit to him. It's tasteful, not cringey.

journey.section: What you need for a sand ceremony
journey.quote: A small table. Draped in linen, at waist height, placed so guests can see your hands and you are not turning your back on them.
journey.reaction: Sensible. Waist height suits me, but my mother uses a walking frame and couldn't stand at a table on sand. Nothing here says what to do if one of the family pouring can't stand or walk far.

journey.section: A sand ceremony at a beach or destination wedding
journey.quote: Before you settle on the setting, put these questions to the venue or, for a public beach, the local council.
journey.reaction: I like a checklist of questions to ask. That's practical. But they're all about wind and the sand itself. The question I'd ask first is whether Mum can actually get down onto the beach, and it isn't on the list.

journey.section: A sand ceremony at a beach or destination wedding
journey.quote: Ceremony approval. Does a ceremony on this beach need a booking or approval, and who arranges it?
journey.reaction: Yes, this is the 'who is responsible' question I'd want answered. Glad it's asked, even if it isn't answered.

journey.section: A sand ceremony at a beach or destination wedding
journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel and vendors with you as a single point of contact, working in your time zone.
journey.reaction: One person, in our time zone. That's the 2am-in-Italy worry covered, at least in principle. I'd still want a name and a phone number before I believed it.

journey.section: A sand ceremony and the legal words
journey.quote: If you marry overseas, the marriage must be valid under the law of the country where it happens, and valid under Australian law had it taken place here, to be recognised in Australia, so speak to a lawyer to confirm your certificate.
journey.reaction: Very glad this is here, with a government link. It's the most useful sentence in the article for me. The two long legal quotes above it are heavy going on the iPad, but I understand why they're there.

journey.section: Planning the ceremony around the pour
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: In writing before we commit. That's what I want to hear. Nothing about deposits or who holds them, but this is a sand article, so I won't hold that against it.

unanswered_questions: Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked, and who would that be?
If we book through Wedded Concierge, how are deposits paid and are they protected?
Are quotes in Australian dollars, and are any fees agreed in writing up front?
Who do we ring if something goes wrong on the day, overseas, out of hours?
How do older or less mobile guests get to a beach or garden ceremony spot, and can they be seated for a family pour?
Does the Wedded Advisor arrange the celebrant and any beach or council approval, or do we?
would_share_with: My husband (the parents' pour section, and the overseas legal paragraph)
Sophie, to say I'd like to pour with her father

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit. Start the conversation with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: It says the right things: one person, in writing, before we commit. But it doesn't tell me whether 'start the conversation' means a phone call or a form, and I won't fill in a form without knowing someone will ring me. I'd more likely ask Sophie to click it and pass my questions on.

top_3_changes:
Add an access question to the beach checklist, as a question only. Old: "- **Ceremony approval.** Does a ceremony on this beach need a booking or approval, and who arranges it?" New: "- **Ceremony approval.** Does a ceremony on this beach need a booking or approval, and who arranges it?
- **Access for older guests.** Can guests who use a walking frame or wheelchair reach the ceremony spot, and is there seating close to the table?"

Give the parents' pour a direction for family who can't stand. Old: "[Each set of parents pours a thin layer. The couple then pour their own colours together.]" New: "[Each set of parents pours a thin layer. If a parent or grandparent would rather stay seated, bring the carafe and vessel to them. The couple then pour their own colours together.]"

Remove the ambiguity of 'sits well after'. Old: "The pour sits well after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order." New: "The pour fits neatly after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order." Same fix in the FAQ. Old: "The pour sits well after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome." New: "The pour fits neatly after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome."

open_questions.question: This persona wants to know whether 'Start the conversation' leads to a phone call. Can the CTA say how contact happens, using only wording the brand already approves? I have not suggested wording because I can't confirm a phone option exists.
Deposits, fees in AUD and protection of payments are this persona's biggest worries but are deferred by the brand. Is there an approved page to link for those, rather than adding claims to this post?
